summary: Under a cap the template says to reserve the adversarial voices as one batch and pass one reservation id, but the native and each outside pass take their own `--start adversarial-review` token. Reservations are one-shot, so the second voice's start is always refused with BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED.
evidence: lib/ship-budget.ts:324 `if (r.state !== 'open') throw ... (one-shot)`; adversarial.md:91-93 requires a separate --start per attempt. Scratch repro: first admitReviewStart returned tok-1, second printed 'outside start REFUSED: ... reservation parent-r1 is already consumed by start tok-1 (one-shot)'.

summary: unreservedDispatches only matches review-log rows against the parent ledger's reservations. Review dispatches a delegated child ran under its own ledger's reservations are flagged as unreserved, so the parent's `close` stops with BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED and status=incomplete after any delegated segment that contains reviews.
evidence: The function iterates only `l.reservations` and never consults l.handoffs or child ledgers. Scratch repro with a review row reserved in a child ledger: 'parent close exit 3 ... BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED (role=review step=9 ...) STOP: reason=budget_check_skipped dispatches=1'.

summary: Under a cap admitReviewStart refuses any --start without a reservation, regardless of skill, but the design-review-lite start instruction used by /ship was not updated to reserve or pass --reservation. Frontend diffs under a cap fail at Step 9.
evidence: lib/ship-budget.ts:321 `if (!reservation) throw ... BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED` (no skill filter); design.ts:46 `gstack-review-log --start design-review-lite` with no --reservation; only review, review-fix-check and adversarial-review were updated.

summary: rebuildLedger builds a claude meter without sessions or config_dir, and cmdResume ignores --session when the meter type is unchanged. After a rebuild the Claude meter reads 0 forever, so used never grows and the admission cap is not enforced.
evidence: Scratch repro: session journal with 5,000,000 usage tokens; `resume --record rec --rebuild-from-record --session <id>` printed 'BUDGET: used=1000 ...' and 'sessions after rebuild: undefined'.

summary: The per-branch marker gates every `gstack-review-log --start`, including standalone /review. A capped /ship run that stopped and was never resumed or closed blocks all reviews on the branch with BUDGET_CAP_REACHED, and a live capped run blocks standalone /review with BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED.
evidence: admitReviewStart throws on `l.stopped` or a missing reservation for any skill once activeLedger(marker) is set; the marker is only removed by close or by a cap of none.

summary: Under a /ship token cap, Step 9's `gstack-review-log --start design-review-lite` has no --reservation instruction, but admitReviewStart refuses any start without one, so capped /ship runs with frontend changes fail at the design review.
evidence: lib/ship-budget.ts:321 throws BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED when !reservation; DIFF_REVIEW_STEP (lib/ship-budget.ts:41) lists design-review-lite as a dispatch; the template adds --reservation only for review, review-fix-check and adversarial-review. Repro: after `gstack-ship-budget start --token-cap 25M --meter estimate`, `gstack-review-log --start design-review-lite` printed BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED and exit=1.

summary: cmdResume only rebinds Claude sessions when the meter kind changes, so `resume --session <new>` (the RECOVER path 'in a fresh session') keeps metering the old session; the new session's spend is never counted and the cap is not enforced. rebuildLedger likewise never restores meter.sessions.
evidence: `const meter = pickMeter(o) ?? l.meter.contract.meter; if (meter !== l.meter.contract.meter) { ...bindClaude... } else readMeter(l, o, false);` Repro: start bound to session A, `resume --session B`, B journal with 5,000,000 input tokens, then `check` printed `BUDGET: used=0 ...`; the ledger's sessions stayed [A].

summary: The cap marker is per branch and only `close` removes it, so a capped /ship that stopped or was abandoned makes every later `gstack-review-log --start` on the branch (including standalone /review, which never passes --reservation) exit 1 until someone resumes or closes that run.
evidence: bin/gstack-review-log routes --start through admitReviewStart whenever $BRANCH-ship-budget.json exists; activeLedger only skips closed or uncapped ledgers; a stopped ledger throws BUDGET_CAP_REACHED. Repro: with a capped run active, `gstack-review-log --start review` exited 1 with BUDGET_CHECK_SKIPPED.
